Constant-speed uniqueness follows from one-dimensional positive arclength. Strict likelihood-ratio ordering proves the all-temperature inequalities. The endpoint-singular integrand difference has integral exactly 4/3 after rescaling and yields two endpoint contributions 8/3; expansion of the normalized inverse quantile gives the stated interior coefficient. A separate beta rescaling proves the boundary profile locally uniformly; dominated convergence yields the universal beta quantile. The standalone verifier passed 61 supplementary checks; no computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A recent general numerical scheme for Sinkhorn length geodesics creates a concrete need for an exact strong-regularization benchmark. The global strict temperature order, nontrivial Beta(3/4,3/4) interior profile and exponentially separated endpoint mass and time scales quantify where discrete geodesic chains must resolve sharp features. They are structurally motivated by the geometry and are not merely a renaming of the prior metric. The result does not assert full solver convergence or many-point generalization.
